macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: Wall Street tech sell-off deepens
items.summary: The S&P 500 fell 1.1% and the Nasdaq Composite dropped 2.1% on Friday as semiconductor and other large technology stocks continued to retreat. The Dow declined 0.3%, while Brent crude rose 3.7% and the 10-year Treasury yield slipped to 5.09%.[1]

items.title: Inflation keeps pressure on the Federal Reserve
items.summary: Recent U.S. inflation data exceeded expectations, with September CPI up 3.7% year over year and core CPI up 2.6%. Markets are pricing limited odds of an October rate increase but increasingly expect additional tightening later in the year.[4]

items.title: Fed enters blackout ahead of October meeting
items.summary: The Federal Reserve’s communications blackout has begun ahead of its October 27–28 policy meeting, removing official guidance while investors assess inflation and rate risks.[5]

items.title: AI investment concerns dominate markets
items.summary: Investors are questioning the durability and financing of the AI build-out after a sharp decline in semiconductor and technology shares. CoreWeave’s roughly $50 billion debt burden has become a particular focus for traders.[3]

items.title: Meta and Tesla earnings take center stage
items.summary: Meta Platforms and Tesla are scheduled to report quarterly results Wednesday, beginning a week of major technology earnings that could determine whether the recent AI-related sell-off intensifies or stabilizes.[2]

items.title: China plans tighter controls on strategic technology exports
items.summary: China is preparing restrictions or bans on exports of 40 technologies, including artificial intelligence, semiconductors and solar power, as competition with the United States intensifies.[1]

items.title: Tesla unveils new Roadster
items.summary: Tesla unveiled a new Roadster sports car featuring advanced engineering capabilities, including the ability to thrust itself briefly into the air.[1]

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin trades above $82,000 after volatile session
items.summary: Bitcoin was reported above $82,000, with intraday gains ranging from roughly 0.24% to 0.80% in different market snapshots. Short-term holders moved more than 50,000 BTC to exchanges, including about 29,500 BTC transferred at a loss, indicating elevated selling pressure.[2][4][6]

items.title: Crypto liquidations approach $934 million
items.summary: Nearly $934 million in cryptocurrency positions were liquidated across approximately 167,400 accounts during a period of heightened volatility, with Bitcoin and Ethereum among the most affected assets.[5]

items.title: OCC expected to finalize GENIUS Act stablecoin rule by October’s end
items.summary: U.S. Comptroller of the Currency Jonathan Gould reportedly said the OCC’s final rule implementing the GENIUS Act is expected very soon and no later than the end of October.[4]

items.title: Russia plans restrictions on direct peer-to-peer crypto transactions
items.summary: The Bank of Russia reportedly plans to require individuals to conduct direct crypto transactions through authorized intermediaries starting July 2027 and has prohibited transfers from digital accounts to self-custodial wallets.[4]

items.title: UK sanctions crypto payment platforms over alleged Russia-linked sanctions evasion
items.summary: The United Kingdom imposed sanctions on Cryptomus, Heleket and TokenSpot, alleging links to Russia-related sanctions evasion. TokenSpot reportedly transferred more than $950 million to sanctioned exchanges and networks.[2]

items.title: Polygon releases Bor update addressing denial-of-service vulnerabilities
items.summary: Polygon Labs released Bor v2.10.3, which fixes two medium-severity denial-of-service vulnerabilities associated with BlockSTM V2 parallel block execution.[4]

items.title: Deutsche Bank reportedly preparing Bitcoin and Ether custody service
items.summary: Deutsche Bank reportedly plans to launch a cryptocurrency custody service within the next few weeks, initially supporting Bitcoin and Ether.[1]

items.title: DTCC launches tokenization service for securities
items.summary: The Depository Trust and Clearing Corporation reportedly launched a tokenization service whose first supported batch represents approximately $30 trillion in underlying securities.[1]

items.title: Digital-asset investment products record weekly net outflows
items.summary: CoinShares reportedly recorded $434 million in net outflows from digital-asset investment products for the week, with strong U.S. inflation data cited as a factor.[1]

items.title: U.S. government-linked address moves about $1 billion in seized Bitcoin
items.summary: An address labeled as holding funds seized from the Bitfinex hack transferred 12,267 BTC, valued at approximately $1.01 billion, according to blockchain monitoring reports.[2]

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 campaign early access begins
items.summary: The campaign mode for Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 launched for players with preorder early access. The full game is scheduled for October 23, with DMZ mode arriving October 20.

items.title: Indie developer cancels public demo over AI-cloning concerns
items.summary: Alliance Arts canceled a planned public demo for Drunken Goddess Reflux, citing concerns that its distinctive gameplay and presentation could be quickly copied using AI tools. The developer will instead hold limited closed sessions.

items.title: Congress proposal would require permanent game-ownership options
items.summary: A proposed U.S. bill would require publishers to offer consumers a permanent purchase option rather than relying exclusively on subscriptions. The initiative follows concerns about server shutdowns and the shift away from physical game distribution.

items.title: Hillthorn announced for November 10 release
items.summary: The card-based detective game Hillthorn received a new trailer and a November 10 release date for Nintendo Switch, PC, and mobile devices.

items.title: The Wolf Among Us Remastered Switch version delayed
items.summary: Telltale delayed the Nintendo Switch release of The Wolf Among Us Remastered indefinitely, saying additional development time is needed to meet its quality goals.

tech_news.query: What are the most important technology news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major product launches, company news, and significant tech industry developments. Exclude AI-specific news.

items.title: GlobalFoundries to build two New York chip plants
items.summary: GlobalFoundries plans to open two semiconductor plants in New York, backed by $21 billion in Japanese financing. The expansion would increase U.S. chip-manufacturing capacity.

items.title: Florida wins ruling over social-media restrictions for children
items.summary: Florida secured a key court ruling allowing enforcement of a law targeting children’s use of social-media platforms, a development with broader implications for technology regulation and platform liability.

items.title: Lowe’s expands drone delivery through DoorDash and Wing
items.summary: Lowe’s is partnering with DoorDash and Alphabet-owned Wing to deliver home-improvement supplies by drone, with delivery times advertised as short as 20 minutes.

items.title: NVIDIA RTX Spark laptops begin shipping
items.summary: NVIDIA’s Arm-based RTX Spark platform is reportedly shipping in Windows laptops from six manufacturers, marking a new push into high-performance Windows computing hardware.

items.title: Apple tightens App Store rules on nonconsensual intimate imagery
items.summary: Apple updated its App Store policies to prohibit applications that generate nonconsensual intimate images, strengthening restrictions on abusive image-generation tools.
